newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Petrobras rebounds, up 2.16 pct.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Petrobras rebounds, up 2.16 pct.

text.p: Preferred stocks of state oil firm Petrobras recouped early sharp losses to rise 2.16 percent to 212.50 reais in mid-afternoon trade, brokers said.
Traders said the market's mood improved as players absorbed news of a court sentence ordering Petrobras to pay a 3.4 billion real fine to a minority shareholder of Petroquisa, a company subsidiary.

Trade in Petrobras, which was suspended Thursday following a request from Brazil's Securities and Exchange Commission (CVM), resumed today after Petrobras sent a statement to the stock exchanges saying it had appealed the court order and that it was not under obligation to pay the fine yet.
Brokers think that even if Petrobras ends up paying a fine, it is unlikely to pay such a large amount.
"The value of the fine is too high. We don't think Petrobras will have to pay that much," a trader said.
In the statement, the company also said it was unlikely to be liable for such a large fine.
Petrobras common stock was also firm in afternoon trade. Its voting share was up 3.57 percent at 174 reais after having surged more than seven percent earlier.
The share is moving on expectations that foreigners will be allowed to buy Petrobras voting stock when a new oil law is approved, traders said.
Petrobras preferred has been the second most traded stock on the Sao Paulo bourse today, accounting for 17.4 percent of trade. It usually accounts for seven percent to eight percent.
The Bovespa index of the 49 most active stocks was up 1.9 percent at 83.301 points.
Total turnover was lower than usual at 322.6 million reais ($310.1 million).
